phase: constant-cell padding (document: traffic analysis / Var-CNN, DeepCorr)
what: every QUIC datagram on every hop is framed [len:u16][payload][zero pad] to one cell size, so inner packet sizes do not leak on any link (DAITA alone shapes only client<->first-hop)

lab.tool: tools/managed_test.py (padding is always on; no flag)
lab.note: each layer sends exactly one datagram size (audited via AVPN_CELL_AUDIT); wire packets still vary by QUIC header jitter and receive offload, which is why the proof is at the datagram layer

unit: src/run.rs frame/unframe round-trip; a receiver that does not strip gets the padded blob (mutation); an over-long length prefix is rejected
cost: constant cells roughly double the overhead of small packets; fixed per chain; off by default
always_on: no command, flag or preference turns padding off; avpn init always signs cells=true into every hop's profile

refusals.data_plane: advanced-vpn refuses a config without cells=true (tools/test_cli.py)
refusals.connect: avpnctl refuses to connect a chain signed before padding existed, before any host change (tools/test_controller_json.py)
refusals.enroll: enrolling an unpadded bundle is refused
refusals.still_allowed: reset, guard and info still load such a chain, so the kill switch can always be cleared to re-sign it
refusals.version_mismatch: the v0.3.3 release binary refuses a current padded profile (exit 1), and the current binary refuses an unpadded one, so an old and a new hop never run mismatched
